units.source_en: ### Commitment and advancement

paragraphs.source_en: Once we've learned the key facts about our industry and customers, it’s time to zoom in again and start revealing our idea and showing some product. The bad news is that this invites nefarious compliments. The good news is that since we have the beginnings of a product, we're now in a position to cut through the false positives by asking for commitments.

units.source_en: Once we've learned the key facts about our industry and customers, it’s time to zoom in again and start revealing our idea and showing some product.
The bad news is that this invites nefarious compliments.
The good news is that since we have the beginnings of a product, we're now in a position to cut through the false positives by asking for commitments.

paragraphs.source_en: In sales, moving a sales relationship to the next stage is called "advancement". It's like pushing a customer into the next step of your real-world acquisition funnel. They'll either move forward or make it clear that they're not a customer. Both are good results for your learning.

units.source_en: In sales, moving a sales relationship to the next stage is called "advancement".
It's like pushing a customer into the next step of your real-world acquisition funnel.
They'll either move forward or make it clear that they're not a customer.
Both are good results for your learning.

paragraphs.source_en: When you fail to push for advancement, you end up with zombie leads: potential customers (or investors) who keep taking meetings with you and saying nice things, but who never seem to cut a check. It's like your startup has been friend-zoned. Thankfully, you caused it, and that means you can fix it. It's a consequence of being clingy and fearing rejection. By giving them a clear chance to either commit or reject us, we get out of the friend-zone and can identify the real leads.

paragraphs.source_en: As I use them in a customer learning context, commitment and advancement are separate concepts which overlap quite a lot and tend to appear together.

units.source_en: As I use them in a customer learning context, commitment and advancement are separate concepts which overlap quite a lot and tend to appear together.

paragraphs.source_en: - Commitment — They are showing they’re serious by giving up something they value such as time, reputation, or money.

units.source_en: - Commitment — They are showing they’re serious by giving up something they value such as time, reputation, or money.

paragraphs.source_en: - Advancement — They are moving to the next step of your real-world funnel and getting closer to a sale.

paragraphs.source_en: Commitment and advancement often arrive hand-in-hand. For example, to move to the next step (advancement), you might need an introduction to your contact’s boss (reputation commitment). As such, they are functionally equivalent for our purposes and I’m going to blur them into one concept for the following sections.
